page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n4 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel x86_64 cores with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

The underlying Intel processor includes advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_tile, AMX_int8), alongside cryptographic accelerations like AES and SHA_NI. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1561.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1807.0. However, multi-core capabilities fall into the lower tier, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3213.05 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4100.0.

Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with uncached read and write speeds of 32.36 GB/sec and 21.01 GB/sec respectively, placing its memory subsystem in the bottom 25% of tested configurations. The instance lacks local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data. Given its balanced resource ratio and average single-threaded performance, the n4-standard-4 is suited for moderate general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 6.53 GB/sec, or lightweight text processing and single-threaded compression tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated Intel x86_64 vCPUs (2 physical cores) and 16.0 GB of RAM. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. The CPU features advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1807.0 and a static web serving throughput of 6.53 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are relatively weak, with uncached memory read speeds of 32.36 GB/sec and a multi-core Geekbench score of 4100.0. This resource profile makes the instance suitable for moderate, non-intensive workloads such as static web serving, basic text processing, and lightweight single-threaded applications, while highlighting performance tradeoffs in memory-intensive or highly parallelized compute tasks.
